evidence: production_batch_runner.py:104 `proj_single, proj_agent = _project_criteria(ctx, {c["id"] for c in (*single, *agent)})` fans project criteria into every run keyed off ctx.repo_root

test_production_batch_runner.py:269-293 test_size_ladder_escalation_through_runner_equals_bespoke builds routed_ids from route_criteria(ctx) with repo_root=None (real repo) on BOTH sides, so the extra project.portability appears on both and the equality holds — no explicit isolation

advisory.finding: Activating project.portability at the real repo root changes the ambient effective-criteria set for the whole suite; the two isolated built-in-assertion tests are correctly fixed, but other unmodified callers (e.g. the ProductionBatchRunner 'equals-bespoke' tests and route_criteria splits) only survive because both compared sides derive from route_criteria(ctx) on the same real repo — a symmetric-by-accident invariant that is fragile to future edits.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Replace the rubric prose/heading greps (test_finding_threshold, test_finding_schema_markers, test_client_shape_matrix, test_omission_guard, test_project_configuration_guard) with behavior assertions on the criterion's observable output (e.g. that a plan with a portability violation surfaces a finding and a shape-agnostic plan does not), or gate the grep on a real non-human consumer of those tokens.
evidence: assert "## Finding threshold" in body ... for element in ("cited plan mechanism", "materially different supported client shape", "causal failure mechanism", "observable breakage scenario")
assert marker in body for markers 'location: str'...'criteria: list[str]' (test_finding_schema_markers, line 205)
assert 'Silence about portability is not a finding' in body (test_omission_guard, line 241)
search_files for 'Finding threshold' / 'Required finding fields' / 'Supported client-shape matrix' returns ONLY the rubric .md and this test file — no parser/validator consumes these tokens
Rule-5 litmus: the grepped token is a real contract only if a NON-HUMAN consumer branches on it; an LLM is not a non-human consumer, so a prose/heading grep guarding wording is a change-detector
advisory.finding: Five rubric-contract tests (test_finding_threshold, test_finding_schema_markers, test_client_shape_matrix, test_omission_guard, test_project_configuration_guard) assert the literal prose wording of the rubric body, an LLM-consumed instruction artifact. No non-human consumer (parser/validator/CI runner) reads these headings or strings, so they are change-detectors: any behavior-preserving rewording of the rubric breaks them without changing observable behavior.
scenarios: A future edit rewords 'observable breakage scenario' to 'observable failure' or reorders the matrix without changing what the LLM criterion does — these tests fail despite no behavior change

The rubric body prose could name a finding field ('scenarios: list[str]') that diverges from the real schema in passes.py/contracts.py, and the grep would still pass — it tests text, not the field contract
